readerValues.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Tax Law bachelor studies how taxes work in law, business and society. Students combine legal interpretation and argument with economics, financial accounting and ethical questions about taxation. Teaching is in Dutch, with some English.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: No close UCR comparison was found for the documented Tax Law curriculum. UCR combines genuine legal, accounting and taxation-policy study, but its strongest options do not sustain the fiscal legislation and case application developed in the confirmed Leiden core. The revised final-year uncertainty remains separate from this academic judgment.

curriculum.limitation: Verified subset: 155 of 180 EC. Credits for the remaining 25 EC of advanced fiscal courses, the final-work requirement and third-year progression conditions still need confirmation for the revised curriculum. Moot Court is confirmed as 5 EC, but its relationship to final work is unresolved. The older third-year table cannot supply these details. Elective study must meet Leiden’s level and approval rules and avoid overlap with required courses.

comparisonScope.label: No close UCR comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The 26 documented components totaling 155 EC: 120 EC of revised first- and second-year legal and fiscal study, 30 EC of genuine open study, and the documented 5-EC Moot Court requirement.
comparisonScope.excluded: The remaining 25 EC of revised required study, its final-work allocation and assessment, full progression and any unconfirmed new-cohort Moot Court entry or assessment rules. No older thesis or equal course weights are assumed.
